# Ferrari

## Identity
Ferrari should be treated as a category-correct reference system for supercar-editorial, using editorial, luxury, cinematic as the guiding visual attitude.

## Use When
- supercar-editorial
- supercar
- racing
- editorial automotive
- automotive
- luxury

## Core Visual Rules
- Keep the composition faithful to automotive, luxury expectations.
- Let editorial, luxury, cinematic shape typography, spacing, surfaces, and motion.
- Make the result feel native to automotive, luxury rather than generic premium marketing.
- Favor editorial pacing and chapter-like sections over generic feature grids.

## Category Alignment
- Family: external
- Categories: automotive, luxury
- Industries: automotive, luxury
- Product types: supercar-editorial
- Style keywords: editorial, luxury, cinematic

## Capabilities
- Supports editorial pacing, chaptered storytelling, and image-first narrative rhythm.

## Compatible Support Systems
- Cryzo 2 can be referenced only for minor supporting polish, never as an overpowering second primary.
- Apple can be referenced only for minor supporting polish, never as an overpowering second primary.

## Avoid
- used cars
- vehicle inventory
- marketplace
- dealership app
- generic AI-generated SaaS hero stacks
- purple-on-dark Bolt defaults

## Prompting Note
- If this reference is selected as the primary system, it controls composition, typography attitude, palette behavior, CTA styling, imagery direction, and motion language.
- Do not describe the output as inspired by another brand unless that other brand was explicitly selected instead.
- Treat this file as binding build guidance, not as an optional moodboard.
